_comment: Machine-readable search config. /seekter-init writes profile/search.json from this template, filling every value from the candidate's own field and geography. Human rules live in profile/profile.md.
_title_filters: title_keep = the title families worth opening, as one case-insensitive regex. title_drop = wrong seniority, wrong discipline, and the other industries that share your job title. Both are field-specific: build them from the candidate's target titles, then add false positives as runs reveal them. Worked example for a product designer: keep 'product design|\bux\b|design system|\bdesigner\b', drop 'junior|intern|head of|director|graphic|motion|industrial|mechanical|fpga|pcb|interior|fashion|textile|game artist' (the last eight are other industries whose jobs are also called 'designer').

freehire._categories: freehire's own taxonomy. A discipline is usually spread over several, so query each one. Run `curl -A seekter 'https://freehire.me/api/v1/jobs/facets?q=<target title>'` to see the categories and counts for this candidate's field.

linkedin._searches: One row per title family x geography. Keywords unquoted (quotes cut recall). geo_id from the table in reference/sources/linkedin.md; 92000000 = Worldwide, 91000002 = EEA. remote = the f_WT=2 filter, which hides hybrid and on-site roles, so add a second row without it for any geography where the candidate can work on-site.

_boards: Job boards for this candidate's field, with how often they are worth a visit. reference/sources/_core.md rates the general ones and reference/sources/ has one file per measured board; niche boards are per-discipline, so ask the candidate which they already read.
